questions.question: Apply public sociology to design a social awareness campaign.
questions.solution_html:
• / Public sociology fosters awareness campaigns that mobilize
  • citizens toward proactive disaster risk reduction efforts.
  • 17a. Disasters are of two main types: natural (earthquakes, floods, cyclones, droughts)
  • and man-made (industrial accidents, wars, chemical leaks).
  • Example: 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami (natural) and 1984 Bhopal Gas Tragedy (man
  • made). / . OR
  • 17b. A hazard is a potential threat that can cause harm. When combined with
  • vulnerability and lack of preparedness, it results in a disaster, such as an earthquake
  • causing loss of life and property.
  • 18a. Disasters have severe social and economic impacts on women, increasing
  • inequality, unemployment, and exclusion from decision-making. They also face
  • heightened caregiving burdens and reduced livelihood options.
  • / . OR
  • 18b. Legal awareness helps individuals understand their rights, duties, and available
  • remedies. It promotes justice, gender equality, and participation in governance and
  • community welfare.
  • 19a. Participatory planning engages communities in disaster management by
  • identifying risks, resources, and solutions. It ensures inclusive, context-based
  • interventions and builds community resilience.
  • / OR
  • 19b. Ethical media conduct during disasters demands accurate reporting, privacy
  • protection, and avoidance of sensationalism. It supports relief coordination and public
  • trust.
  • 20a. Identifying vulnerable populations (elderly, women, children, differently abled)
  • before disasters ensures targeted preparedness and reduces risk through focused resource
  • allocation.
  • / . OR
  • 20b. Mass media plays a vital role in mobilizing resources and volunteers by spreading
  • awareness, coordinating aid, and inspiring public participation in relief activities.
